title: fix(ci): accumulate shard-timings runs until every package has three executions, provisional below that
body:
Part of #22014
Clause-②: no

The shard-timings refresh now keeps adding scheduled runs until every package has been **executed** (not replayed) by at least three of them. Each weight is the median of those executions. When the retained runs cannot reach three for some package, the refresh is still opened, but it is marked **provisional** and does not get refused. The refresh PR body now records each package's run count and its min/median/max.

#22014 stays open after this merges. Its other half is the first multi-run dataset landing on `main` through the refresh lane, which is the seat's act. Nothing in this PR touches `scripts/test-shard-timings.json`.

## Where the one-run dataset came from

The cause was the regeneration loop in `.github/workflows/shard-timings-refresh.yml`, at `803764a36` lines 457-464 (comment at line 372). It ran `break` at the first accumulation that `--check-coverage` passed. Coverage counts a carried weight as covered, so the newest eligible run always passed it by itself. From then on every refresh was one run deep, which is why `provenance.runs` on `main` is `['37262126122']`. The selector was not the cause: it returns every eligible run in the window, up to 24. Retention was not the cause either: 20 eligible runs were in the window. The schedule-only rule was also not the cause. The median machinery from #16473 already worked. Nobody was feeding it more than one run.

## What changed

- **`scripts/measure-test-shard-timings.mjs`**
  - `MINIMUM_EXECUTED_RUNS = 3`.
  - A new `provisional` list sits beside `carriedOver`. It names every package whose weight rests on fewer than that many executed runs.
  - A run counts for a package only when it executed that package. That means a MISS with exit 0, and for a sliced package, a complete slice set from that run. A cached run or a failed run does not count.
  - A carried weight keeps the depth it was measured at. A prior dataset with no `provisional` key never recorded a depth, so its carried weights are provisional. This includes the dataset on `main` today.
  - `provenance.minimumRuns` records the bar.
  - `--spread-out PATH` writes the per-package spread table for the PR body. `renderSpread` builds it.
  - `collectSamples` was split out of `buildDataset`, so the weights and the spread table read the same per-run readings.
- **`.github/workflows/shard-timings-refresh.yml`**
  - The loop now stops only when the latest accumulation both covers the workspace and leaves `provisional` empty.
  - If the candidates run out first, the last covering accumulation is kept and a `::warning::` annotation is emitted. A coverage shortfall is still a refusal, unchanged.
  - The PR body gains a "Sample depth and run-to-run spread" section.
  - The header comments now say why the loop used to stop at one run.
- **`scripts/ci/select-shard-timings-run.mjs`**
  - A note on `coverageReport`: coverage is necessary but not sufficient for the loop to stop.
  - A new self-test battery drives the real regeneration step (see Pins below).

Untouched: the weights' shape (`packages` stays name to seconds), `partition-test-shards.mjs` and its constants, the 25% headroom, the 1.5x red, and the dataset file itself.

## Refuse or provisional: provisional, and why

Triage left this choice to the PR. Each option is weighed on the four axes:

- **Real need (measured).** Today the partitioner and the drift gate read the weights on every Test Core run, and they want the freshest numbers. Only a baseline reader, the per-package ceiling of #16468, is harmed by a shallow weight, and that reader can read the list.
  - Over the 20 eligible runs retained on 2026-10-06, all 72 packages reached three executions, so a provisional refresh should be rare.
  - When one does happen, refusing would throw away 71 packages' measurements because of one package and leave every PR balanced on the old dataset.
- **Long-term soundness.** The workflow's own rule is that a refusal to open "would lose the measurement, which is the exact silent-rot failure this workflow exists to end". With provisional, the producer declares the depth in the file its consumers read. No consumer needs a fallback.
- **Preventing AI mistakes.** The list is machine-readable and lives in the same file as the weights.
  - An empty list and a missing key are kept distinct.
  - A carried weight cannot become non-provisional just by being carried, and a depth that was never recorded counts as not met.
  - The dataset `note` says provisional weights are not baselines.
  - The remaining risk is a future consumer that ignores the list. That is a contract for #16468's ceiling generation to refuse provisional entries. It is stated here and is not built here.
- **Startup focus.** The change is one constant, one list, one provenance number and one optional flag. It adds no new gate, no new exit code and no new workflow. A refusal path would instead add a weekly red job for someone to triage.

## Pins

- `measure-test-shard-timings.mjs --self-test`, battery **`minimum executed runs per package`** (14 cases). It covers:
  - the one-run shape of the current dataset, kept and named provisional;
  - two runs (provisional) and three runs (empty list, present);
  - three runs where one package was replayed in two of them, so that package is provisional;
  - a failed run that does not count, and an incomplete slice set that does not count;
  - all three carry cases: a prior with no list, a prior with an empty list, and a prior that lists the package;
  - a malformed prior list, refused;
  - the bar recorded in `provenance`;
  - the spread table rows.
- `select-shard-timings-run.mjs --self-test`, battery **`shard-timings-refresh accumulation depth`** (11 cases). It lifts the regeneration step's own `run:` block out of the YAML and runs it under `bash -e`. `curl` and `unzip` are stubbed with fixture summaries. The real generator and the real coverage check do the rest, from a scratch tree with a two-package committed fixture. The four legs:
  - **depth reached:** stops at 3 runs out of 4, not at 1, and spec is the median of three;
  - **executed, not replayed:** a replayed run does not count, so the loop takes 4;
  - **provisional, not refused:** with only 2 runs the step stays green, keeps the data, names both packages and annotates;
  - **coverage control:** a lost package still refuses with exit 1.

## The spread format

This is a Markdown table in the refresh PR body, one row per package in the dataset:

`package | runs | min s | median s | max s | max/min | provisional?`

Rows are sorted widest spread first. A carried package shows `carried` instead of invented numbers.

The spread is kept **out of the dataset JSON** because nothing machine-reads it. The partitioner and the drift gate read the weights, and the one machine fact a baseline needs is `provisional`. The only reader of the spread is the person reviewing the PR. This PR's own `pull_request` run of the refresh lane renders the would-be body, table included, into its step summary from the real retained runs, and pushes nothing.

## Per-package reachability of three executed runs within retention

Run-summary artifacts are kept for 1 day. Per-package executed or replayed status was read from each run's `Test Core` timing table ("cache-replayed packages") in the aggregator job logs. Package names below drop the `@objectstack/` prefix.

- **2026-10-05 17:01 to 2026-10-06 15:01** (all 20 eligible scheduled runs in retention when measured):
  - Every one of the 72 packages was executed by at least 3 runs. The newest 12 runs already reached 3 for every package.
  - Tightest: `spec` 7/20, `sdui-parser` 8/20, then `driver-sqlite-wasm`, `formula` and `plugin-hono-server` at 11/20.
  - Busy hours replay a lot: run 37475449497 replayed 54 of 72 packages.
- **2026-10-04 05:31 to 2026-10-05 05:30**, the window the Monday 05:30 refresh reads (sampled, 9 of its 17 eligible runs):
  - Every package was executed by at least 4 of the 9 sampled runs. Tightest: `spec` 4/9.
  - The schedule fired late and irregularly that day, giving 19 runs in 24 hours, not 24.
- **Not reachable: none measured.** `spec` is the package at risk. It is replayed in most hourly runs, and it is exactly the package whose single-run weight (1134.86 s) sat below its executed windows (1573-1651 s). If a quiet window ever leaves it below three, it is named in `provisional` rather than silently recorded from one run.

## How and when the first multi-run dataset reaches `main`

1. This PR merges. The scheduled trigger reads the workflow from `main`.
2. The schedule `30 5 * * 1` next fires **Monday 2026-10-12 05:30 UTC**.
3. The lane opens `claude/shard-timings-refresh-RUN_ID` as `github-actions[bot]`. Without `RELEASE_PUSH_TOKEN` that PR starts no CI by itself, so a maintainer push or update-branch is needed, as the previous refresh needed one. That step is unchanged here.
4. The PR lands through the queue as an ordinary non-governed diff.

The maintainer or the seat could get it sooner with a manual `workflow_dispatch` of the refresh lane after merge. This PR does not do that.

## Evidence (at `68a312380`)

- Self-tests: `node scripts/measure-test-shard-timings.mjs --self-test` printed `self-test OK`, exit 0. `node scripts/ci/select-shard-timings-run.mjs --self-test` printed `self-test OK`, exit 0, in about 9 s.
- Ablations, each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, with the mutation proven on disk and the restore proven (blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty):
  - Loop break reverted to coverage-only: the selector reds with `depth leg: expected the loop to stop at 3 runs, it fed 1`.
  - Generator rule that compares `values.length` with `minimumRuns` deleted: the generator reds with `a one-run refresh was not reported provisional ([])`, and the selector reds on the depth leg.
  - Carry rule inverted: the generator reds with `a weight carried from a depth-less dataset was not provisional ([])`.
- Compose step: run once against a fake `RUNNER_TEMP` for the provisional branch, the full-depth branch and the absent-list branch. The absent list exits 1, as intended.
- Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 52 commands on the actual change set (3 paths vs merge base `803764a36`). All 52 were run. The 51 recorded with exit codes were all 0. `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` printed `dispatch-gates self-test: 1976 cases pass`. Reconciliation with `--ran` reports 52 derived, 52 run, 0 unrun.
- Lint, narrowed: eslint ran on the 2 changed `.mjs` files (the YAML is outside eslint's population) with 0 errors and 0 warnings. The repo config never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, per `eslint.config.mjs`), so this diff cannot move a verdict on any untouched file. The full `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- `skip-changeset`: only the private root package's `scripts/` and a workflow change. No published `files[]` ships them.

## Acceptance notes

- **#16468 contract (not built here).** Ceiling generation should refuse any package in the dataset's `provisional` list, and could also refuse a dataset whose `provenance.minimumRuns` is missing. Both readings are in the file now.
- **Pre-existing, not changed.** When the generator refuses the very first candidate, `unset 'ACCEPTED[-1]'` leaves a sparse array. This path is unexercised, and no failure is measured.
